title: 键盘管理器：开户按钮映射时，任务管理器的输入框无法输入

judgment.rationale: The report gives a 100%-reproducible reciprocal Left Alt↔Left Ctrl mapping that makes Task Manager input fields unusable on Windows 11 24H2 / PowerToys 0.90.1, while disabling the mapping restores input. The exact path still needs current-build replay and event tracing.
evidence: The body specifies both reciprocal mappings and the affected Task Manager input fields.
The author reports the issue occurs 100% of the time and disappears when button remapping is disabled.
The live issue has no comments, assignees, or linked work.
judgment.recommended_action: Replay the reciprocal modifier mapping on a current build and isolate which Task Manager text-entry control stops receiving input.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reciprocal modifier map is a deterministic trigger and may expose interaction between remapped modifier state and elevated/system UI input. The exact event or input-control restriction is not yet proven.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep reciprocal Alt/Ctrl remaps from suppressing Task Manager text input
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reciprocal Left Alt/Left Ctrl mappings may leave modifier state or injected-event handling inconsistent for Task Manager's input controls. This is an unconfirmed hypothesis; the control's integrity context and event sequence must be checked.
plan: Replay both reciprocal mappings on the reported Windows 11 24H2 setup and a current PowerToys build.
Compare typing in Task Manager's input field with a standard Notepad edit field while recording the remap event sequence and process integrity level.
Trace the first lost or misclassified key event in the Keyboard Manager hook path before changing behavior.
Add a focused regression test for reciprocal modifier mappings and the observed input/control boundary.
verification: Task Manager input fields and ordinary text fields both accept text with the reciprocal map active.
The two modifier mappings still work as configured and do not leak unintended shortcuts.
Disabling the mapping continues to restore the original behavior.

confidence.rationale: The trigger and symptom are deterministic, but there is no evidence yet whether the failing point is Keyboard Manager state or a Task Manager/integrity boundary.

issue_context.summary: With Left Alt mapped to Left Ctrl and Left Ctrl mapped to Left Alt, Task Manager input fields reportedly stop accepting text; disabling the remap restores input.
known_information: Reported on PowerToys 0.90.1, Windows 11 Pro 24H2 build 26100.3775.
The author says the failure occurs 100% of the time with the reciprocal button mappings active.
No comments, assignees, or linked work are present.
inferences: The reciprocal modifier state may interact with Task Manager input handling or its integrity boundary.
issue_context.analysis: The scenario is specific enough for a focused current-build replay. The hypothesis is deliberately provisional; no root cause should be claimed until the failing event and control boundary are identified.
initial_investigation: Read the full Chinese issue body and confirmed there are no comments.
Checked live labels, assignees, and linked work; none was found.
The reported Windows build and reciprocal mapping are sufficient to create a targeted reproduction.

design.title: Keep reciprocal Alt/Ctrl remaps from suppressing Task Manager text input

actions.label: Replay reciprocal Alt/Ctrl map in Task Manager

reproduce.title: Test text input with reciprocal Left Alt and Left Ctrl mappings
prerequisites: Current upstream main or current build
Task Manager and a standard text editor
steps: Configure Left Alt→Left Ctrl and Left Ctrl→Left Alt in Keyboard Manager and enable the mappings.
Try typing ordinary text in a Task Manager input field and in Notepad.
Disable only the mappings and repeat both input tests.
Record whether the fields have different integrity levels and which key events are observed.
reproduce.expected_result: Text is accepted in Task Manager and ordinary text fields with the reciprocal map active, or a precise control-boundary limitation is isolated.
